description: One outstanding note or loan: who lent it, what is still owed, what it is secured on, and which account on the borrower's chart carries the liability. ERPNext's own Loan module is a lending product; this is the other side — a handful of notes a holding company owes, tracked well enough that nobody has to open a filing cabinet to answer 'what do we still owe on the sorter'.

fields.description: What this note is called in conversation, e.g. 'Umpqua Bank - GP Graders Automatic Defect Sorter'. Unique per borrower; the docname is built from it and the company abbreviation.
fields.label: Note Name

fields.description: The entity that owes the money.
fields.label: Borrower

fields.description: Who is owed: a bank, an estate, an individual. Free text rather than a Link, because the lender on a family note is usually not a Supplier on this site and creating one to record a loan would put a name into the buying module that has no business being there.
fields.label: Lender

fields.description: Active until it is closed. Paid Off, Refinanced and Written Off are set by close_note_payable, which records the disposition in the event history rather than only flipping this field.
fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Active
Paid Off
Refinanced
Written Off
Superseded

fields.description: The note that replaced this one, when a refinance rolled it into a new instrument. Following the chain forward lands on the note that is still owed.
fields.label: Superseded By

fields.description: Where the paper lives: a Governance Document docname, a file reference, or a plain description of the physical original. Free text on purpose — the promissory note for a 2003 family loan is often not a document this site holds.
fields.label: Document Reference

fields.description: What was originally borrowed. Never changed by a payment — the running balance is Principal Outstanding.
fields.label: Original Principal

fields.description: What is still owed on principal. Maintained by record_loan_payment; it is a convenience figure, and the account named in Notes Payable Account remains the authoritative balance.
fields.label: Principal Outstanding

fields.description: Annual rate, as a percentage. 0 with an interest type of Zero is a genuine family note rather than a missing value.
fields.label: Interest Rate

fields.description: When the last payment is due. Read by link_asset_to_note to work out the note's tenor, so an asset financed by it can be held to the same term.
fields.label: Maturity Date

fields.description: The scheduled payment, principal and interest together, where there is one.
fields.label: Payment Amount

fields.description: The Notes Payable liability account on the borrower's chart. Debited for the principal half of every payment recorded against this note.
fields.label: Notes Payable Account

fields.description: Debited for the interest half of a payment. Optional here; record_loan_payment takes an override, and refuses rather than guessing when neither is set.
fields.label: Interest Expense Account

fields.description: The asset this note financed, for a secured note. Setting it also points the asset's cost profile back at this note, so depreciation_note_alignment_check can see whether the two terms have parted company.
fields.label: Related Asset

fields.description: Every payment and every disposition, with the Journal Entry that carries it and the balance it left behind. Written by the tools; editing it by hand does not move a balance.
fields.label: Events

fields.description: What a successor trustee would need: how the note arose, what secures it, what was agreed verbally, where the original is.
fields.label: Notes

name: Note Payable
